comment: This principle is framed mainly as rationing, which concedes scarcity where the first answer is often to grow capacity. But capacity and funding constraints are real — especially at state and district level — so scaling cannot always meet demand. We recommend designing for scale and graceful degradation: scaling (elastic and distributed) where capacity can grow, funded by usage-linked contribution; degrading gracefully rather than locking users out where resources are genuinely finite; and guarding against abuse rather than legitimate use (e.g. changing "protected from overuse" (p.55) to "protected from abuse").

reviewer.organisation: CoWEAVE - Medtronic LABS; eGov Foundation; Open Healthcare Network Foundation

public.text: This principle is framed mainly as rationing, which concedes scarcity where the first answer is often to grow capacity. But capacity and funding constraints are real — especially at state and district level — so scaling cannot always meet demand. We recommend designing for scale and graceful degradation: scaling (elastic and distributed) where capacity can grow, funded by usage-linked contribution; degrading gracefully rather than locking users out where resources are genuinely finite; and guarding against abuse rather than legitimate use (e.g. changing "protected from overuse" (p.55) to "protected from abuse").
